title: I need your help.
content_type_note: NOT a horror story episode. This is a creator-appeal / community-post video from a 2D horror-animation channel (demonetization plea). Its outlier status comes from the personal-crisis format, not horror storytelling. Useful for the horror lane only as: (a) channel-voice / avatar-narrator format, (b) a behind-the-scenes production breakdown as B-roll, (c) the emotional-appeal script skeleton. Do not use as a horror story structure reference.

devices: first-person plea, 4 words, full stop = sincere, not clickbait-shouty
zero topic information: curiosity + concern ('what happened to them?') drives clicks from existing subscribers
breaks the channel's normal story-title pattern, so it stands out in the sub feed
title_pattern.notes: Classic creator-crisis title. Works because it is rare on the channel and leans on parasocial loyalty of 1.84M subs; would not work for a new faceless channel without an audience.

thumbnail.composition: Left ~2/3: real screenshot of YouTube Studio 'Your channel remains ineligible for monetization' page (sidebar, red prohibition icon, orange cone); a large tilted red rubber-stamp 'DEMONETIZED' with a warning triangle slapped across it. Right 1/3 on solid black: the channel's anime avatar (blond bowl cut, pink shirt), waist-up, worried brow, teeth clenched, looking at the viewer.
thumbnail.text: 'DEMONETIZED' in distressed red stamp capitals, the only large text; Studio UI text is legible but small (proof, not headline)
thumbnail.colours: White/grey UI field, saturated red stamp + red prohibition icon, orange cone, black panel behind a pastel-pink avatar - red on white is the only loud colour
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Huge stamp vs. small UI text; small calm avatar vs. loud red verdict. Real UI screenshot vs. drawn character = 'this is real, not a story'.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Instant read in one word (DEMONETIZED) + receipts (real Studio page) + a familiar mascot face showing distress. For fans it signals a real-world event about the creator they follow; it also baits creator-economy viewers outside the niche who click every demonetization drama.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: My channel has been demonetized. About a month ago, my Hindi channel was demonetized first.
hook.verbatim_0_14s: My channel has been demonetized. About a month ago, my Hindi channel was demonetized first. Now, my original main channel has also been demonetized, and the reason is apparently because my Hindi channel had already been demonetized.
hook.device: Bad-news-first cold open: the worst fact as the very first sentence (matches thumbnail and title, no intro/branding), then an absurd-sounding cause ('demonetized because the other channel was demonetized') that invites outrage. Visual proof (stamped Studio screenshot) on screen from frame 1.

beats.summary: 'My channel has been demonetized.' Explains the Hindi channel went first, then the main channel was demonetized because of it; DEMONETIZED stamp on Studio screenshots as proof.
Not a solo creator: a real animation team paid monthly; multiple animators' livelihoods at risk. B-roll switches to finished hospital-scene animation to show the team's work.
Animation is hard money: drawing frame after frame all day for low income; B-roll is a frame-by-frame lip redraw in the software.
Big sub count does not mean big money because of payroll; 8 years running the company, months of losing money after paying salaries, kept going for fans and love of the craft.
2D animation is a poor business; AI makes survival harder; 'I refuse to give up' - human-made animation still has value.

Worked with professional animators, BG artists, character designers worldwide; pays fairly; goal is TV/theatrical quality free on YouTube; investing ever more. Visuals: layered compositing breakdown of a polished occult scene.
'And then suddenly, this happened.' 8 years reduced to nothing; 10+ animators affected; enormous powerlessness.
The 90-day wait is not the main issue; 3 months of salaries would mean personal debt; alone he could get a job, but there is a whole team.
Patreon/merch are not enough; considered quitting animation entirely but cannot walk away from 8 years.

YouTube doesn't see the channel's potential even as quality improves and investment is highest ever; now considering closing the company (stakes peak). B-roll: upcoming horror episode animatic (under-the-bed story) as a teaser.
'So, I'm asking my fans for a favor' - if you can reach YouTube's internal team, please help my channel. Ends on the avatar reaching toward the viewer over an animatic creature shot; no outro.

pacing.speech_density_note: Continuous, calm, slightly formal VO (reads like a translated/written statement) with almost no pauses; sentence lengths 10-25 words.
pacing.avg_shot_length_note: Background B-roll changes ~39 times in 274 s (avg ~7 s); the avatar overlay never cuts away - it only swaps among ~4 gesture poses roughly every 4-8 s. Animatic section (3:24-4:34) is much faster (~2.5 s per panel) to build energy toward the plea.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-45 s: each paragraph opens with a new stake ('it's not just me', 'many people might think', 'and with AI', 'and then suddenly, this happened', 'I am currently considering whether to close down').

transcript_source: YouTube auto-subs (en-orig), converted to timestamped lines; full text in research/library/transcripts/tpS0hPca-fk.txt
techniques_worth_copying: Persistent narrator avatar on the right third over changing full-frame B-roll: one character asset with lip-flap + 3-4 gesture poses carries a 4.5-minute video cheaply; B-roll can be anything.

Receipt-first cold open: the claim in sentence one is backed by an on-screen 'document' with a stamp graphic - transferable to horror as 'case file / police report / found note' with a red stamp (CLASSIFIED, MISSING, DECEASED).
Rubber-stamp text device in the thumbnail: one distressed red word over a realistic UI/document = instant read at mobile size.

Title as a first-person plea with full stop ('I need your help.') - sincere register contrasts with typical shouty titles; adaptable as an in-story narrator line for horror ('Please don't open this.').
Escalating-stakes paragraph structure: every 30-40 s a new, bigger stake, peaking just before the CTA (closing the company) - same skeleton as a horror escalation.

Visual 'process reveal' B-roll (layout -> line -> values -> colour -> composite, layer toggles, zoom in/out of a canvas) keeps the eye busy during talky sections; a code pipeline can fake this by animating SVG layers in sequence.
Pacing acceleration in the last minute: B-roll cuts drop from ~7 s to ~2.5 s right before the ask.

Ending on a teaser of unreleased horror content (under-the-bed animatic, 'DON'T LOOK UNDER HERE' wall writing, silhouette in a doorway) - curiosity for the next episode embedded in an unrelated video.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: High for the format, low value as a horror template. The appeal-video structure is trivially codeable; the B-roll here is real production art which we would replace with our own SVG scenes.
assets: One SVG narrator avatar (flat cel shading, 4 gesture poses: neutral, hand-on-chest, open-palm side gesture, reach-to-camera) with 3-4 mouth shapes for lip-flap driven by TTS phoneme/amplitude timing
Mock 'document/UI' card component (rows of grey text bars, icon, heading) + red rubber-stamp SVG with grunge mask, rotate -8 deg, slam-in animation (scale 1.4 -> 1 with 2-frame shake)
Layered SVG scenes that can be revealed layer by layer (sketch strokes via stroke-dashoffset, flat fills, shadow pass, light glow) to imitate a 'production breakdown'
Fake app chrome (dark workspace frame with a floating canvas) to zoom the scene in/out
Grey animatic style: desaturated line art with cyan/magenta flat key colours and handwritten cut labels (A1, B2) for teaser panels
motion: Avatar fixed right-third, idle breathing (1-2 px y sine) + pose swaps on sentence boundaries
Background canvas: slow Ken Burns pushes (2-5% over 10-20 s), occasional zoom-out to show the 'workspace'
Hard cuts on sentence starts; cut rate speeds to ~2.5 s in final 60 s
code_only_remake_needs.audio: Single calm TTS VO at ~165 wpm, no music bed or very low pad, no SFX except stamp thud at 0:00
code_only_remake_needs.captions: None burned in in the reference; for shorts we would add word-level captions
